page: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a general-purpose cloud compute instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system exposes 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes modern vector instruction support such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache, providing strong computational density across all threads.

The hardware configuration features 256 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally provisioned via an integrated 3840 GB NVMe SSD, eliminating external volume latency for primary data tiers. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators. For network connectivity, a single complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the deployment.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional compute and input/output capabilities. In single-core and multi-core evaluations, Geekbench scores of 2,767.0 and 27,795.0 place it in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Raw computational throughput is further evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 83,864.35 and a clang software compilation benchmark of 64,042.0. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 496.98 GB/sec, while write operations achieved 190.5 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 104.09 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier database operation throughput in PassMark testing.

With its combination of 64 dedicated compute threads, 256 GB of memory, and 3.8 TB of fast local NVMe storage, this server offers efficient resource density for multi-tenant backend environments. The balanced resource ratio avoids the overhead of specialized tiers while delivering high execution speeds for production databases, large-scale continuous integration pipelines, microservices clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Vultr vx1-g-64c-256g-3840s is a high-capacity instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute lineup, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs from 32 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 256 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory configuration, accompanied by 3840 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The system features AVX-512 vector extensions and lacks dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier for Geekbench single-core (2,767.0) and multi-core (27,795.0) metrics, as well as PassMark database operations and large-block memory bandwidth. Delivering substantial throughput without specialized pricing tiers, this server fits large relational and in-memory database engines, comprehensive CI/CD build farms, high-concurrency web serving, and enterprise container hosting.
